subject: social_science

concepts.title: Crisis of the Mughal Empire
concepts.section: The Crisis of the Empire and the Later Mughals
concepts.definition: The era of administrative and financial decay in the imperial state after 1707, characterized by failing central oversight and the rise of local kingdoms.
concepts.key_idea: Decline of central authority due to wars, weak successors, and noble factions.
question_patterns: Explain the reasons for the decline of the Mughal Empire.
What were the main factors leading to the crisis of the empire?
How did the later Mughals lose control over their governors?
Describe the impact of peasant revolts on the Mughal administration.
Why did the efficiency of the imperial administration break down?

solution_steps.explain: Aurangzeb's long wars in the Deccan exhausted financial and military resources.
Later Mughals could not control powerful mansabdars and provincial governors.
Peasant and zamindar rebellions over high taxes challenged imperial authority.

concepts.title: External Invasions of the 18th Century
concepts.section: The Crisis of the Empire and the Later Mughals
concepts.definition: Military incursions by rulers from Iran and Afghanistan that resulted in the looting of the capital and the weakening of the sovereign's power.
concepts.key_idea: Foreign raids by Nadir Shah and Ahmad Shah Abdali drained Mughal wealth.
question_patterns: Who was Nadir Shah and what was the impact of his invasion?
Describe the plundering raids of Ahmad Shah Abdali.
How did foreign invasions weaken the Mughal Empire?
What wealth did Nadir Shah take from Delhi?
When did Ahmad Shah Abdali invade north India?

solution_steps.explain: The ruler of Iran sacked Delhi in 1739, taking the Peacock Throne and immense riches.
Ahmad Shah Abdali invaded north India five times between 1748 and 1761.

concepts.title: Rajput Watan Jagirs
concepts.definition: Semi-autonomous hereditary estates where local chieftains maintained governance while maintaining a formal link with the central throne.
concepts.key_idea: Rajput rulers enjoyed internal autonomy in exchange for imperial service.
question_patterns: What were watan jagirs in the context of Rajput rulers?
How did Rajput kings like Jai Singh extend their territories?
Explain the role of Sawai Raja Jai Singh in the eighteenth century.
What was the significance of Jantar Mantar?
How did Maratha campaigns affect Rajput principalities?

solution_steps.explain: Hereditary lands where Rajput rulers were permitted considerable autonomy.
Rulers like Ajit Singh and Jai Singh sought governorships of rich provinces like Gujarat and Malwa.

concepts.title: Sikh Political Organization
concepts.definition: The evolution of the Panth into a sovereign political body through the creation of the Khalsa and organized military units called misls.
concepts.key_idea: Transformation of Sikhs into a militant state-building community.
question_patterns: How were the Sikhs organized into a political community?
What was the role of Guru Gobind Singh in Sikh state-building?
Describe the administration established by Banda Bahadur.
What are misls and how did they function?
Explain the significance of the Dal Khalsa.

solution_steps.explain: Guru Gobind Singh instituted the Khalsa in 1699 to resist oppression.
Sikhs organized into jathas and misls, collectively known as the Dal Khalsa.

concepts.title: Rakhi System
concepts.definition: A security arrangement where farmers provided one-fifth of their harvest to the Dal Khalsa for safety.
concepts.key_idea: Protection tax levied by Sikh bands on cultivators.
question_patterns: How much tax is paid under Rakhi?
Calculate the Rakhi tax for a produce of {produce}
What is the 20 percent tax for protection?
Find the amount due to the Dal Khalsa for {produce}
Determine the protection fee for a harvest of {produce}

solution_steps.explain: The total agricultural output is produce.
Rakhi tax is 20 percent of the produce.

concepts.title: The Maratha State
concepts.definition: A robust regional power established in the Deccan that used mobile warfare and specific levies to expand its influence across the subcontinent.
concepts.key_idea: Rise of Marathas under Shivaji and the Peshwas.
question_patterns: How did Shivaji establish a stable Maratha kingdom?
What was the role of the Peshwas in the Maratha state?
Describe the military organization of the Marathas.
Why were other rulers hostile towards the Marathas?
Explain the administrative system developed by the Marathas.

solution_steps.explain: Shivaji used warrior families and peasant-pastoralists to challenge Mughals.
Under Peshwas, the capital moved to Poona and Maratha influence reached Delhi and Bengal.

concepts.title: Chauth
concepts.definition: A levy representing a quarter of the agricultural tax gathered by Maratha forces from neighboring regions.
concepts.key_idea: Maratha tax consisting of 25 percent of land revenue.
question_patterns: Calculate the chauth for a revenue of {revenue}
Find the chauth tax when the revenue is {revenue}
What is the chauth for a collection of {revenue}
How much chauth is due on {revenue}
Determine the chauth for a land revenue of {revenue}

solution_steps.explain: The total land revenue is revenue.
Chauth is 25 percent of the land revenue.

concepts.title: Sardeshmukhi
concepts.definition: A supplementary charge of nine to ten percent given to the chief tax officer within the Deccan province.
concepts.key_idea: Additional levy of 9-10 percent paid to the head revenue collector.
question_patterns: Calculate the sardeshmukhi for a revenue of {revenue} at {rate} percent
Find the sardeshmukhi levy for {revenue}
What is the sardeshmukhi amount for a revenue of {revenue}?
Determine the levy for the head collector on {revenue}
How much is the 10 percent sardeshmukhi on {revenue}?

solution_steps.explain: The revenue is revenue and the rate is rate.
Sardeshmukhi is the percentage of revenue.

concepts.title: The Jat State
concepts.definition: A group of prosperous farmers who consolidated their influence near Delhi and Agra, eventually forming a fortified state at Bharatpur.
concepts.key_idea: Jat consolidation under Churaman and Suraj Mal.
question_patterns: How did the Jats consolidate their power under Churaman?
Describe the prosperity of the Jat state under Suraj Mal.
What was the significance of the Bharatpur fort?
How did the Jats utilize architectural styles from Amber and Agra?
What regions were under the political control of Suraj Mal?

solution_steps.explain: Churaman acquired territories west of Delhi; Suraj Mal established Bharatpur.
Jats were prosperous agriculturists with trading centers like Panipat.
